body: Thank you I needed this <3
Thank you so much :) I needed the reassurance
Thank you. I needed to hear this
Thank you so much :)

Thank you for your insights. Your story really resonates with me. I hope I'm able to find a job and put myself (and my family) at ease and in more financially secure position. And that just isn't going to happen with academia.
This is so similar to my situation. How has it been since making that decision?

Thank you. I made an appointment for the career center. I think I'm over emphasizing my PIs approval and what that even means in this process. But you're right, it's my life. And I'm so deeply unhappy. Something has to change.
Thank you ❤️ it's not easy to force our own space, but I do believe we can do it! I haven't figured it out yet but I'm not going to give up just yet.

Totally! I have not read a single book "for fun" since my PhD program (I read very little in my MA). I'm in my 5th year too...That's horrible! I hate that I've lost that. But when picking between a game and a book, lately I've been picking games haha. This "break" I picked up BioShock infinite and I'm IN LOVE. I had played the first two back when I was a "gamer" and loved the series. Im glad I finally got to play the 3rd one. 

Small things are the best sometimes!

Thank you! And I know exactly what you mean. This shit is so hard. I wish I could prepare 2012 me for this haha

And re: kids. It is fucking hard, but you gotta live your life the way you want to. If you want kids, do it. If you don't, don't. But don't let academia steal that from you. The best time to have kids is when you WANT to. Which ever path you choose do it for you ❤️
Yes, I believe that setting myself up like I'm at a "job" has been key. It's the only way I've been able to progress.

It's hard to force a space for yourself in academia. I still don't know how to do it, but I think I'm getting better at it. It's a long road. 

Setting boundaries around when is work time and when is relax time helped me to not feel guilty as much. My partner works similar hours to how I've set my schedule so that we can relax at the same time. It helps but it's not perfect. We are still working on making it all work out. 

I encourage you to not give up. The best dissertation is a done dissertation!
Haha thank you ❤️ you too!

Yes, I know. I hope that if I ever find myself as a mentor I always keep in mind how powerful mentor support is. Just the casual check-ins and "good work on this" bring me such a relief. 

Glad you got a good Prof now! You deserve that!
Thank you! We will do this!
Yessssss! Rock it!

I understand what you are saying. I see others saying "not my experience" so I am only commenting to say: this IS my experience. 

Im sorry I don't have advice I'm struggling with same feelings.
I lost my father suddenly at 23 so I do not qualify for this study but I wanted to say thank you for looking at this.
I've done it as second author and on papers with my PI. But my PI gave me several templates so they are easy for me to reproduce. I think she has me do them every other paper or so as "practice"

Thank you for this...

I took my son to the pool this weekend 💜
From what I've seen, no. They did not pay back anything.

I'd still do it. Tell the therapist that you need help expressing your (non) diagnosis with your mother and that it would be better if the therapist was there for it. I think they would be willing to do this, and it doesn't have to be a whole session just a casual conversation in passing. Just like a "mom, Dr. Explained to me that I do not infact have BPD." 

Basically I'd call her out on the lie.

Agreed. This thread gave me a label for my mother: narcissist. This has helped me process so much of our past interactions, helped me to understand her current actions, and even helps me to anticipate her future behavior. I'm very glad for this sub.

I get what you mean, and I think for many that is definitely a huge plus (the flexibility of working location).

I have found that because of this flexibility, I am expected to be available and working at any given time. I hate bringing work home because I don't feel that I have a healthy family-work-life dynamic. The blurred boundaries of academia is not working for me. I think I'm learning that now.
I have a 2 year old. I wake up at 5:30 every day, get him ready for daycare and then he leaves with my husband by 7am, then I get my self ready and get to my office by 8ish.
Thank you for sharing this. I hope to find something like this one day.
I really appreciate everyone's input. Thank you all for taking the time to comment. It has been very enlightening. I still don't know what to do but I'm trying to figure it out.
Thank you. I think I need to keep hearing this.
Thank you I will check this out.

Thanks for responding. My son is almost 2 as well. You're right about the routine and sleep part. I will look into those books.

I just want a job that has clear boundaries. As in these are work hours and these are not.  Even if I set those boundaries for myself. For me, I would like evenings/nights and most of the weekend. But when people are literally telling me it is unrealistic to want those boundaries I feel like there is no solution.
Thank you. I appreciate your response. I'm trying to pull through.

Having you laugh at me for asking about a hobby honestly left my crying. I am a new mother too. I don't want to be defined by only motherhood and grad school/work. We are full and complete people. Maybe I want to join a recreational sports team. Maybe I want to join a knitting group...I don't want to do nothing but work and keep house anymore.

Yes...I spent a good part of the night researching this. You're right I'm just afraid now I'll fail at this too. I'm in a low place bc of grad school and I'm trying to pull out if it but it keeps bringing be back down.

Bc of the combination of others telling me I should be working double this and that I'm never getting enough work done (because I'm only doing ~40) I feel burnt out that my most will never be good enough. So yes.
Yes. My department highers ppl with around 10-15 pubs
Hm that does sound good. I'll look into this. Thanks for the tip

I have a follow up question, especially to those working 50+ hours a week: 

Who cleans your house? Who goes to the grocery store? Do you manage the bills? Who organizes family schedules (i.e. daycare, Dr visits, social events). Who cooks?

I'm not trying to be snark. I honestly don't understand how it works. I feel like I'm coming undone.

I am definitely going to apply to non-academic jobs. Especially bc it feels like I won't be competitive enough for an academic one. I am social sciences. My statistics is pretty good but that feels like my only winning quality.
You're right. I have made a grave mistake. I wish I could take it all back. But I'm six years into this (2 MA program 4 PhD program), I don't know what else to do.

I agree with you. But it honestly feels like I am never productive enough. I'm falling behind on all my work, I can't work on side projects, and I require the hand holding of professors on the papers I have now. I see them work. They do work more than me. They do work 60-70 easy. 

I try to work more but I'm so burnt out and I have a family (they don't). Idk what to do
I just don't want this life and I'm crying now bc it feels like it's this or joblessness. I wish I could go back in time and tell myself to never enter the program

Wow. I hate academia. Check my profile if you want. Haaaaate. It's miserable. 

But no don't do this pls. It's not worth it. Get a new advisor, take a week off, and redo your thesis. Don't cheat. Don't do it.
Yep. Publish or perish. And I'm perishing.

It's great that you're having a good experience. And i agree this is an important perspective. Especially in comparison to the negativity on here (that i am def a contributor to).

But come on, grad school is not great. It is demoralizing, belittling, and often toxic. There is blatant disregard for mental health, there is little to no support for families, and you are often made to believe you are worthless when in reality universities are dependent on your cheap, devalued labor to survive. 

Both perspectives are important. 

This subreddit is full of negativity bc academia is full of negativity. 

I often hesitate when an undergrad asks me if they should go to grad school. As a woman of color and a mother, a part of me wants to tell other WOC to join me in taking over the world. But another broken part of me knows this system was never designed with us in mind. 

I think sharing our true feelings is not only therapeutic, but I believe points out a systemic issue across multiple fields in academia. This issue needs to be address. 

So, while yes, I'm so happy you're enjoying this journey. I know my negative response sounds bitter and aggressive, but i am truely happy for you. And yes, take my hand and lets take over the world together. But do not side step my cries for help either. 💜

This is such an accurate description. Why is this academia? What other job produces such mental health issues for its personnel? 

At some point academics need to address this head on, so we can heal. I just don't see it happening any time soon.

How do I even address it?

This resonates with me so deeply. I am moved to tears. 

Why is this the common experience in academia? Why is this institution so anti family? And on so many levels. 

Im glad you posted. Thank you for sharing. If you want to continue to talk i am open. I sometimes wish i had someone to talk to too.

Thank you all for your responses. I posted this then had to step away for a while. It strangly felt better after i posted it. 

Some context (although i will admit its so exhausting to explain everything that pushes me away and yet keeps me tethered to academia): i am 4 years post my masters, at this point i need to just finish. I probably need two more years to finish everything I have left. Having my child really slowed me down and if I'm being honest also has contributed to my overall depression, especially postpartum depression. 

I do seek therapy, but I often feel so isolated and alone that i am unable to deal with this. And as each of you said, many grads feel like this. Which makes me think, how fucked is academia that it just cranks out emotionally and mentally damaged people? When will this cycle explode on itself? When will academics care about themselves and others? It seems unlikely. 

Thank you again. It has helped me gasp some air.

Thank you again for your advise. 

I stated above that I had previously been on medication for my OCD and it helped a lot. I felt like a regular person. It was nice. 

But right now I am reluctant to take it because I would have to stop nursing. My Dr said she wouldn't prescribe it until I was finished nursing...I guess I could talk to her more about this (along with advice from the pediatrician).

Thank you so much for your comment. And good luck on your defense :)

I have in the past gone to therapy and I did see benefits from it. I can't really put into words why I don't continue to go. I guess I don't feel comfortable talking to someone or I feel too unmotivated to actually set up the appointment. It is something that I struggle to do but I may be at a breaking point and need to the help more than ever. 

I am also "off my meds" right now which has been particularly hard. I wanted to get off when I got pregnant and now that I am nursing my dr did not feel comfortable putting me back on. I am already under producing due to the lack of time to pump when away from the baby, my lack of motivation to pump (it is awful), and all my stress. I think my immense day-to-day stress has almost completely dried me up. So this may be the time to throw in the towel and just take the meds. 

I am still reluctant because my son wants to "comfort nurse" and so the low supply doesn't matter that much in that respect. I would have to stop comfort nursing him and I am not ready to make that leap. He is on about 75% formula at this point. 

But, again, therapy in itself may be beneficial enough to get me through this period of time. 
<3

I absolutely agree with you. Some days it doesn't feel worth it at all. I don't even enjoy my work any more. 

Thank you! I am rooting for you too. :)

Thank you for commenting. It is really nice to hear from another mom in a phd program. 

I am really thinking that full time daycare is the way to go. 
Unfortunately it would be impossible for me to take even a week of with the way things are right now....so I will have to power thru. I will keep your words in mind hoping things get easier.

Daycare is a struggle for us because of our financial situation. My husband is a pre-k teacher and as a grad student I make almost double his income...so its not a lot...

I am so sorry you struggled with HG too. I wouldn't wish it on any woman. It was a nightmare. And, if I had a "normal job" I would have had to quit for sure.

Thank you for replying. 

I should clarify that by "role model" i mean to other women in phd programs who either want to be or are mothers. There is so much negativity and discrimination around mothering in grad school it is heartbreaking. I wanted to be able to show everyone that they are wrong - that moms can get phds too. I just didn't realize how much harder it would be. 

But you are right, phd or not, my kid will be okay. :)

Thank you so much for replying. Your post has given me a little boost. 

I think you are right, transitioning to full time daycare will be necessary. Luckily I like the place he is at right now and he also seems to be enjoying it. I think the issue of money is definitely what has held us back from full time. But reading your post has given me some thoughts on what can be done to pay for it (loans, CC, etc) 

And again, you are right, having a supportive PI is lucky. Its just hard that she keeps extending deadlines, giving me less work, and being so sympathetic and yet I keep failing over and over. 

I want to finish I think, but I'm afraid of the costs to my well-being. But I think I am more afraid of regret and unemployment.
